text:
aj: Heads-up — while onboarding rwdx-13b-quant-v2 I saw a reproducible divergence after a cold-start + KV restore when context > 12k. Putting notes / repro here.

aj: Steps to repro (local):
```
# start the server with int4 payloads
RWD_MODEL=rwdx-13b-quant-v2 ./serve --quant=int4 --kv-restore=true --max-context=65536
# feed a long prompt (12k+ tokens) then continue streaming 1k tokens
curl -sS -X POST http://localhost:8080/generate -d '{"prompt": "<12k tokens priming...>", "stream": true, "seed": 42}'
```

aj: Observed behavior: first 10–12k tokens match float32 baseline exactly, then after the KV-restore boundary the sample distribution shifts — outputs become shorter and insert repeated filler phrase after ~200 tokens. Perplexity jumps reported by the eval harness.

sara: :eyes: Do you see the same with int8?

aj: int8 is fine — no shift. int4 cold-start (fresh process, cold cache, then restore from snapshot) triggers the divergence. Warm-start (server never restarted) is fine too.

devon: Could be a alignment/stride problem when we pack cached KV in int4 lanes. Did you check the prefill token-to-position mapping?

aj: Yep. I diffed the positional indices and they align for the first 12k tokens. The mismatch appears only when the snapshot is loaded and we run the quant-dequant path. Small excerpt from the token-checker log: 
```
[KV-LOAD] shard=3 restore_ok=true entries=12288
[KV-VERIFY] idx=12287 pos=12287 tok=0x7a3f ok
[KV-VERIFY] idx=12288 pos=0 tok=0x4c1a MISMATCH
[ESTIMATE] quant-scale=0.00321 bias=0.00012
```

tanya: Is the snapshot created on int4 or on float? i.e., we snapshot after quantization or before? That matters for how we restore alignment.

aj: We snapshot post-quantization (the publish step writes quantized KV to disk). Repro steps include loading that file.

devon: Two hypotheses: 1) an off-by-one in shard indexing when switching address base during restore; 2) wrong byte-order assumption for partial lanes in the int4 packer (end shards get padded and we mishandle tail nibble). Both could explain a single index shift at boundary.

sara: I can run a quick binary-checker against the on-disk file to look for padding patterns. If it's nibble-padding we should see a repeated value in last 16 bytes of each shard.

ci-bot: Test run queued: rwdx-13b-quant-v2/kv-restore-check (id: CI-9117). Expect results in ~12m.

aj: Also saw degraded log-prob slopes on beam scoring after restore — beams collapse faster. I'm attaching the small eval snippet I used (prompt truncated):
```
--prompt--
[PRIMING: 12000 tokens truncated for log]
--continue--
seed=42 
beam=5 
max_new_tokens=512
```

tanya: If it's padding, int8 wouldn't show it because each byte is standalone. int4 packs two values per byte so tail handling is special. Good call.

devon: I'll instrument the packer and add an assert to check that restore reads the exact number of nibbles. If the file length % shard_grain != 0, fail loudly.

aj: Quick workaround for teams: set KV-restore=false for int4 snapshots until we confirm. That keeps cold-start behavior consistent albeit slower.

sara: Will triage and run the binary-check now. If I find a pattern I’ll paste hexdump.

aj: Filing internal ticket RW-ML-2034 for tracking. Tagging @devon and @tanya.

tanya: If we confirm nibble tail bug, patch plan: 
- tighten packer/loader invariants
- add file format versioning field (1 byte) to snapshots
- add CI binary check that loads snapshot and performs token-level diff against float baseline

devon: Agreed. Also add a regression test that cycles cold-start restore with varied context lengths (4k, 12k, 32k) and multiple seeds.

ci-bot: CI-9117 finished: failures=1, logs: https://ci.internal/runs/9117 (summary: mismatch at shard 3 tail).

sara: hexdump excerpt: 
```
00000f70: ... 9b 7a 3f 4c 1a 00 00 00 00 00 00 00
00000f7c: ... 9b 7a 3f 4c 1a 0f 0f 0f 0f 0f 0f
```

sara: See repeating 0x0f tail nibbles in restored file for int4. That looks like padding used during write, but loader is not trimming it — we treat padded nibble as real token value after unpack.

aj: Nice find. So loader should mask off tail nibbles using the saved `valid_entries` count. But we don't persist that? I thought snapshot header contained entry_count.

tanya: Header exists but earlier format (v1) stored entry_count in 32-bit words; for int4 pack we need entry_count in nibbles. Looks like the packer wrote nibble_count but the loader read word_count for older v1 header. Classic format-version mismatch.

devon: Fix: extend header with new field nibble_count and bump file format to v2. I'll prepare a small PR to the packer/loader and include compatibility shim: if v1 then convert word_count->nibble_count with formula.

aj: Can we also add an on-disk magic + checksum to detect accidental truncation? That would have flagged this earlier.

tanya: Yup, add CRC32 and magic GUID. Put it in v2.

sara: I'll rerun CI once PR lands. Also will add a short doc to onboarding checklist: "verify int4 snapshot restore across context boundaries".

aj: Thanks all. For visibility: metrics to watch after fix — per-token KL against float baseline, beam-collapse point, and token-repeat frequency in 1k window after restore.

devon: PR opened: https://git.internal/rwd/p/pkr/+/4567 — includes header bump, nibble_count, CRC, and regression test.

ci-bot: CI run queued for PR 4567.

aj: Great. If anyone hits other odd cold-starts with quant snapshots, drop them here. :thumbsup:
